pr_body:
This PR adds a native AO for pipewire and closes #8569.

The original code has been written by @Oschowa which was extended by me. (See the different commits)
@Oschowa did not propose the PR themselves as they were experiencing vsync jitter with this AO.
For other users however this AO works as good as or better than the existing ones, and they have been using it for some time with custom builds.

When running on a native pipewire system this AO saves intermediate steps through libpulse and pipewires pulseaudio server.

* [ ] `set_pause`
* [x] `uau` wonders if there is a problem in accurately reporting the remaining buffered audio.

No, it doesn't work with this property and it won't. PW_KEY_NODE_RATE is used to suggest a sample rate.


Here's some changes: [ao_pipewire-mpv.patch.txt](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/files/7736225/ao_pipewire-mpv.patch.txt)

> @etircopyh Is this patch supposed to fix the issue or just do some cleanups? If it is supposed to fix it, could you point out the specific part doing that. If not, could you provide a way to reproduce the issue?

It does fix the issue and doing a bit of cleanup along the way. It does not interfere with anything. You can reproduce the issue with current state of PR with playing some 44.1 kHz file and running `pw-top` where you'll see something like this: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26657892/146575232-71cb4dfe-9ed7-4036-8f43-0ba5432b9e2d.png)
Device doesn't follow file's sample rate.

With fix you'll have this: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26657892/146575524-d2a0edea-4bcb-4cc8-8aa0-28f980cb3027.png)

And yeah, you need to have [44100 in your allowed-rates in your `pipewire.conf`](https://github.com/etircopyh/arch.conf/blob/c070fdbe91637a21abbfa7867852746a06e96f43/dotfiles/user/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf#L22).

> If it is supposed to fix it, could you point out the specific part doing that.

It's the part that sets PW_KEY_NODE_RATE as I said before.

Thanks for the information. I messed up `PW_KEY_NODE_RATE` vs `PW_KEY_AUDIO_RATE`...
I'll incorporate your changes.

A few more questions:
* Why is "PW_KEY_NODE_ALWAYS_PROCESS" needed?
* Why are some of the properties that are set to `ao->client_name` set in `pw_properties_new()` and some with `pw_properties_set()`?

> Why is "PW_KEY_NODE_ALWAYS_PROCESS" needed?

As far as I understand it's supposed to make life easier for people that have no device node or are playing around with virtual sinks/sources, like connecting them together, etc. [Some explanation](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/issues/1761#note_1123327). It seems like there's more to come on this one.

> Why are some of the properties that are set to ao->client_name set in pw_properties_new() and some with pw_properties_set()?

I kind of looked it up but I think it's to make sure these properties don't collide with ones that pipewire sets. Because pw_properties_set() does set a property and overrides it.

> > Why is "PW_KEY_NODE_ALWAYS_PROCESS" needed?
> 
> As far as I understand it's supposed to make life easier for people that have no device node or are playing around with virtual sinks/sources, like connecting them together, etc. [Some explanation](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/issues/1761#note_1123327). It seems like there's more to come on this one.

Good, thanks for the explanation!

> > Why are some of the properties that are set to ao->client_name set in pw_properties_new() and some with pw_properties_set()?
> 
> I kind of looked it up but I think it's to make sure these properties don't collide with ones that pipewire sets. Because pw_properties_set() does set a property and overrides it.

Yes it would replace existing values. But as we are constructing the properties from scratch there should be no conflict.
After the properties have been populated and send to Pipewire there is no difference.

Just wanted to say I've been testing this patch since the latest changes, and while I can't comment on the code, I can say it works as advertised. No audio glitches as far as I can tell. Hopefully someone will have time for a more thorough review soon. Thank you for making this PR.

issue_context.title: PipeWire support
issue_context.body:
[PipeWire](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire)

Due to pulse backend being quite unstable causing constant desyncs and stuttering I propose to add PipeWire support which is already proven to be more reliable and most importantly have more user-friendly developers.

PipeWire now is under active development. Fedora 34 intent to make it [default.](https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Changes/DefaultPipeWire) While I understand that PW's API docs is far from completeness this should be at least considered for future implementation. Basically PipeWire can already be used with mpv and any other PulseAudio/JACK app, as all audio from them is routing to PW if one installed. But that still leaves bugs of libpulse and pulse-server in-between. So it would be definitely step forward for Linux audio processing.

[PipeWire Overview](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/master/doc/overview.md)
[PipeWire Architecture](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/master/doc/architecture.md)
comments:
There has been a proposed PR for a PipeWire audio output last year: #7902
It was not considered for inclusion at the time and IIRC it wasn't quite feature complete either.

> pulse backend being quite unstable causing constant desyncs and stuttering

That's news to me.
I thought the official stance from the PipeWire devs was that clients targeting pulse and not writing native integration was a reasonable long term strategy.

> I thought the official stance from the PipeWire devs was that clients targeting pulse and not writing native integration was a reasonable long term strategy.

Huh? I didn't know it, any reason to think that?
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/wikis/FAQ#what-audio-api-do-you-recommend-to-use

> [gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/wikis/FAQ#what-audio-api-do-you-recommend-to-use](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/wikis/FAQ#what-audio-api-do-you-recommend-to-use)

"for now" doesn't run with your "long term". That's why I said:
> this should be at least considered for future implementation.

FWIW, a while ago i took the original pull request for the pipewire backend and added some improvement and fixes - mostly format and channel layout negotiation and some error handling. It should be fully functional expect for device enumeration and volume control - which i see no real use for. Anyways, i haven't considered getting it upstreamed, because mpv's ALSA backend works just fine on pipewire, but you can try it if you like: https://github.com/Oschowa/mpv/commit/fddb143282fa74425a8a6f29c9566e51777759d0

> because mpv's ALSA backend works just fine

Yeah, I don't get this "ALSA works just fine" song

FWIW, [PulseEffects](https://github.com/wwmm/pulseeffects) recently made the shift and has rebranded as "Audio effects for PipeWire applications."

PW has a considerable CPU usage advantage over PA. A friend says they can now leave multiple effects enabled in PE and leave it running in the background now (PW was working wonderfully on my old Arch laptop before it died and I could test that). This helps make apps more stable when they are doing a lot of work.

PipeWire is like JACK but with video. wtay has mentioned full-on video synthesis will be possible (like modular synths are in JACK(+LV2)). It would be very neat to be able to use `mpv` in such a video setup, as a source, or an intermediate node (video in, gets effected and displayed, video out, all with a patchbay/node graph for connections like in [Catia](https://kx.studio/Applications:Catia) or [Carla](https://kx.studio/Applications:Carla)).
